body:
This is only somewhat related to #3231, which dealt with two Not filters directly nested. The fix for that was to simply drop both of them. Here we have `<not <or <not <test>> <cat>>>>` so a more substantial fix is probably needed.

We really need a test that demonstrates this to be a framework problem. Running through the console opens up the possibility that either the console is generating an incorrect filter from the `--where` clause or the framework is misinterpreting the filter. For the V2 example, the V2 driver, which translates the NUnit 3 filter to a a V2 filter, also comes into play. Ideally, we want a framework test that creates the filters programmatically and applies them directly. We already have some tests like that, but not for this specific case.
Also sounds related (or at least similar) to nunit/nunit-v2-framework-driver#21.

@okknudsen I think your tests confirm this as a framework bug. Would you be interested in taking it a step further and doing a PR?

I think the failure of the Not filter to search child tests is probably the cause of the problem. It doesn't do so, because finding a child test that matches the filter wouldn't help, since the not would reverse that finding. However, it should do __something__. Off the top of my head it seams that it should expliclicitly search for child tests that pass the filter __under__ the not.

The problem seems to be that, like intuitionistic logic, "not" isn't the opposite of "", and that "not not not" is semantically equivalent to "not", but "not not" isn't to "".

The reason is that "not" has different search behaviors, i.e. it would stop as soon as its inner condition matches, while "" continues searching.

One possible solution might be to detect a situation where a De-Morgan or similar would lead to "not not" and then execute that transformation (and remove the resulting "not not"). But it obviously changes semantics and might [break someone's workflow.](https://xkcd.com/1172/)
@CharliePoole I wouldn't mind trying at least :)

issue.title: Fix issues with Pass method on TestFilter's (issue #3328 )
issue.body:
This fixes #3328 

The problem was the difference in whether we are using a filter to exclude tests or include them when calling `Pass`. In the former case, we want to look back through parents only, but in the latter case, we want to look forward through children as well.

This fix makes sure that this decision is taken by the inner most filters (leafs I guess) by applying De Morgan to ensure that negations are pushed through `AndFilters` and `NotFilters`.

If I forgot something, please let me know. This is my first time contributing.
